domain_label: GPU Training Infrastructure & Cost (LLM Engineering subdomain)
assumptions: no observed dataset or benchmark evidence supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
scope covers GPU rental, VRAM math, distributed training (FSDP/ZeRO), mixed precision, multi-model scheduling, and cost modeling
target workload is fine-tuning or pretraining of LLMs from 1B to 175B parameters
GPU types considered: A100 40/80GB, H100 80GB, L40S, consumer (RTX 4090) on cloud providers

competency_questions.question: What GPU type and count is required to train a 70B parameter model with 8K context in bf16?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GPU_SIZING and VRAM_MATH provide the formula and answer

competency_questions.question: What is the total training cost estimate for a 7B model trained on 140B tokens on H100 spot instances?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COST_MODEL and SPOT_CLOUD provide formula and estimate

competency_questions.question: How is peak VRAM calculated for a 13B model with ZeRO-2 and gradient checkpointing enabled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VRAM_MATH + ZERO_SHARDING + GRAD_CKPT cover all components

competency_questions.question: What checkpoint strategy minimizes recovery loss from spot preemption at minimum storage cost?
When should spot instances be avoided in favour of on-demand for distributed training?
What is the recommended parallelism strategy for a 65B model on 32 H100 GPUs connected via InfiniBand?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ZERO_SHARDING, FSDP_CONFIG, TENSOR_PIPE_PAR, NET_TOPO provide decision logic

competency_questions.question: How does QLoRA reduce VRAM and what accuracy tradeoff should be expected vs bf16 full fine-tuning?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUANT_TRAIN + CA_04 define mechanism and tradeoff

competency_questions.question: How is training loss divergence detected and recovered in a long-running training job?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LOSS_MONITOR + CKPT_INFRA define detection and recovery

competency_questions.question: How is model FLOP utilization (MFU) computed and what does a low value indicate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MFU_MONITOR + COST_MODEL explain formula and bottleneck attribution

competency_questions.question: What makes a training data pipeline GPU-bound vs data-bound and how is the bottleneck resolved?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DATA_PIPE + EC_07 + MFU_MONITOR cover the diagnosis

competency_questions.question: How should concurrent fine-tuning jobs be scheduled on a shared GPU cluster to avoid deadlocks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTI_MODEL_SCHED + EC_06 + FAULT_TOL define the scheduling constraints

competency_questions.question: How does Chinchilla scaling law inform the choice between training a larger model for fewer tokens vs smaller model for more tokens?

glossary.definition: Model Flop Utilization: ratio of achieved FLOP/s to theoretical peak hardware FLOP/s; measures training efficiency
Zero Redundancy Optimizer: DeepSpeed memory optimization that partitions optimizer states, gradients, and parameters across data-parallel ranks
Fully Sharded Data Parallel: PyTorch-native implementation of parameter+gradient+optimizer sharding across data-parallel ranks
bfloat16: 16-bit float with 8-bit exponent (same as fp32); preferred over fp16 for LLM training due to larger dynamic range avoiding overflow
Quantized Low-Rank Adaptation: fine-tuning with 4-bit NF4 quantized base model and bf16 LoRA adapters; enables 70B fine-tuning on single 80GB GPU
DeepMind 2022 scaling law showing compute-optimal training requires equal scaling of model size and training tokens; N_opt proportional to D_opt proportional to sqrt(C)
Cloud GPU instance offered at 60-90% discount with risk of preemption when provider reclaims capacity; requires checkpoint-on-preemption
IO-aware attention algorithm using tiling to reduce memory from O(N^2) to O(N) and increase arithmetic intensity; mandatory for long-context training
NVIDIA high-bandwidth intra-node GPU interconnect; required for efficient tensor parallelism within node; bandwidth 600 GB/s vs 64 GB/s PCIe

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for GPU training infrastructure work units derived from practitioner knowledge of cloud GPU economics, distributed training, and LLM scaling; no measured dataset supplied
grounding_limits: GPU pricing and availability change frequently

source_registry.description: Kleppmann, Designing Data-Intensive Applications — referenced for fault tolerance, checkpointing, and distributed systems patterns
Huyen, Designing Machine Learning Systems — referenced for infra/cost modeling and training infrastructure patterns
source_registry.citation_or_locator: Huyen (2022) Designing Machine Learning Systems, O'Reilly
grounding_limits: general ML systems; pre-dates LLM-scale infra specifics

nodes.definition: Select GPU instance type (A100/H100/L40S/consumer) and quantity by matching model parameter count, activation memory, and batch size to VRAM budget and per-GPU FLOP throughput.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Correct sizing prevents OOM crashes and avoids over-provisioning cost
pros.example: H100 80GB fits 70B bf16 model with ZeRO-3

cons.claim: Prices shift quarterly; locked instance type may no longer be cost-optimal
cons.example: A100 spot price spikes during peak demand

failure_modes: VRAM OOM at runtime
underestimating activation memory for long contexts
ignoring interconnect bandwidth bottleneck
acceptance_tests: VRAM budget formula verified against actual peak allocation
cost-per-token within 20% of target budget

nodes.definition: Compute peak GPU VRAM demand: parameter bytes (dtype×params) + optimizer states (Adam 8×params in fp32) + gradients + activation checkpointing footprint + KV-cache for context length.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Prevents OOM surprises; enables confident batch-size selection
pros.example: 70B bf16 params=140GB; +Adam=280GB; needs 4×H100 with ZeRO-3

cons.claim: Activation memory depends on micro-batch and layer count; hard to predict exactly
cons.example: transformer activations scale as O(seq_len×hidden×layers)

failure_modes: forgetting optimizer state memory (largest component)
ignoring activation checkpoint overhead
KV-cache omitted for long contexts
acceptance_tests: formula reproduces known OOM threshold on reference model
peak VRAM within 10% of profiled actual

nodes.definition: Design training jobs to exploit spot/preemptible GPU instances (60-90% discount) via checkpoint-on-preemption hooks, restart automation, and mixed on-demand fallback.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: 60-90% cost reduction on comparable throughput vs on-demand
pros.example: GCP preemptible A100 at ~30% on-demand price

cons.claim: Preemption rate spikes during peak; can double wall-clock time if unhandled
cons.example: AWS spot interruption rate for p4d can reach 20%/hr

failure_modes: no checkpoint-on-preemption causing full restart loss
relying on single-AZ spot pool
ignoring placement group needs for multi-node
acceptance_tests: preemption simulation test passes within 60s checkpoint save
job resumes from checkpoint within 5 min of restart
revisit_triggers: spot market prices spike above on-demand
new GPU generation spot availability emerges

nodes.definition: Apply DeepSpeed ZeRO stages (1: optimizer shards, 2: +gradient shards, 3: +parameter shards) to distribute memory across data-parallel ranks, enabling training of models larger than single-GPU VRAM.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: ZeRO-3 enables training models 8-64× larger than single-GPU VRAM
pros.example: 65B model on 8×A100 with ZeRO-3 optimizer offload

cons.claim: ZeRO-3 all-gather overhead can reduce throughput by 10-30% vs ZeRO-1
cons.example: inter-node ZeRO-3 saturates 400Gb InfiniBand

failure_modes: unnecessary ZeRO-3 on models fitting ZeRO-1 (wasted comms)
forgetting gradient checkpointing with ZeRO-3
CPU offload causing PCIe bottleneck
acceptance_tests: training step completes without OOM on target model size
MFU (model flop utilization) >35% maintained

nodes.definition: Configure PyTorch FSDP (Fully Sharded Data Parallel) sharding policy: FULL_SHARD vs SHARD_GRAD_OP vs NO_SHARD, wrapping policy per transformer block, and mixed-precision compute/reduce dtypes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Native PyTorch integration with no external dependency; composable with torch.compile
pros.example: FSDP + compile on LLaMA achieves near-linear scaling

cons.claim: Auto-wrap policy choice heavily affects performance; wrong wrap can halve MFU
cons.example: wrapping at linear layers vs full block changes all-gather granularity

failure_modes: incorrect wrap policy causing extra all-gather
forgetting to flatten parameters for older FSDP
mixed-precision mismatch between compute and reduce dtype
acceptance_tests: FSDP training step runs on reference model without error
throughput within 80% of theoretical peak

nodes.definition: Configure automatic mixed precision (AMP) with master weights in fp32, compute in bf16 or fp16, gradient scaling for fp16, and optional fp8 via Transformer Engine for H100 hardware acceleration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: 2× VRAM reduction vs fp32; 2-3× throughput on tensor cores without accuracy loss
pros.example: bf16 training of GPT-3 scale achieves identical loss curves to fp32

cons.claim: fp16 overflow risk on models with large logit variance; bf16 preferred for stability
cons.example: fp16 gradient overflow causes NaN loss spikes in large LLMs

failure_modes: fp16 NaN from loss overflow without gradient scaling
using fp16 on architectures prone to logit explosion
fp8 calibration skew causing underflow
acceptance_tests: training loss curve matches fp32 baseline within 1%
no NaN/Inf in 1000 steps on target model
revisit_triggers: hardware upgrade changes tensor core support

nodes.definition: Design checkpointing strategy: frequency (steps), storage backend (NVMe/S3/GCS), async save to overlap with training, sharded checkpoint format for large models, and restore validation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Prevents full restart loss on preemption; enables experiment branching
pros.example: async checkpoint on 70B adds <2% overhead with NVMe staging

cons.claim: Checkpoint storage cost accumulates; undeleted checkpoints can exceed compute cost
cons.example: 1TB model × 100 checkpoints = 100TB S3 cost

failure_modes: checkpoint corruption undetected until restore
async save race condition corrupting state
no restore validation before training continues
acceptance_tests: restore from checkpoint produces identical loss on held-out batch
async save completes before next checkpoint window
revisit_triggers: model size changes requiring new shard format

nodes.definition: Combine tensor parallelism (split weight matrices across GPUs within a node) and pipeline parallelism (split layers across nodes) for models too large for ZeRO-3 alone or to reduce all-gather communication.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Enables training 100B+ models on multi-node clusters with near-linear scaling
pros.example: GPT-3 175B trained with TP=8 PP=16 DP=96

cons.claim: Pipeline bubbles reduce GPU utilization; PP adds complex schedule and debugging
cons.example: PP=8 with 1F1B schedule has ~15% bubble fraction

failure_modes: pipeline bubble exceeding 20% causing poor MFU
tensor parallelism exceeding NVLink bandwidth causing IB saturation
incorrect micro-batch count for pipeline depth
acceptance_tests: end-to-end training step completes on target cluster without hang
MFU >40% on >4-node job

nodes.definition: Build a cost model: total_cost = GPU_hours × $/hr; GPU_hours = tokens / (MFU × peak_FLOP × 6P); compare cost-per-quality-point across GPU types, parallelism strategies, and cloud providers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Converts technical choices to business metrics; prevents over-spend
pros.example: H100 at 2.5× A100 cost but 3.2× MFU → better ROI for large models

cons.claim: MFU assumptions compound; 2× MFU error doubles budget miss
cons.example: MFU assumes perfect all-reduce; IB-limited jobs often <30% MFU

failure_modes: using peak FLOP instead of MFU-adjusted FLOP
ignoring communication overhead in cost model
forgetting data storage and egress in total cost
acceptance_tests: cost estimate within 25% of actual spend on pilot run
model selects correct GPU type in A/B decision

nodes.definition: Instrument training loops to measure Model Flop Utilization (MFU = achieved_FLOP / peak_hardware_FLOP) and tokens/sec, detect throughput regressions, and attribute bottlenecks (compute vs memory vs communication).

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Catches silent throughput regressions before they compound over long runs
pros.example: MFU drop from 45% to 30% detected in hour 2 vs day 3

cons.claim: MFU measurement depends on correct FLOP count formula; errors mislead
cons.example: attention FLOP count varies by implementation (flash vs standard)

failure_modes: using peak BFLOAT16 FLOP without accounting for memory-bound ops
ignoring communication idle time in MFU numerator
attention FLOP formula discrepancy vs actual ops
acceptance_tests: MFU alert fires within 10 min of 20% throughput drop
profiler correctly attributes bottleneck source in 3 test scenarios
revisit_triggers: new GPU type added with different peak FLOP

nodes.definition: Accumulate gradients over micro-batches to achieve target global batch size (global_batch = micro_batch × grad_accum_steps × DP_degree) without exceeding per-GPU VRAM.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Decouples batch size from VRAM constraint enabling Chinchilla-optimal batch
pros.example: train with global_batch=2M tokens on 8 GPUs via grad_accum=32

cons.claim: Extra accumulation steps proportionally reduce throughput vs data-parallel scaling
cons.example: grad_accum=16 is 16× slower than same batch with 16× GPUs

failure_modes: forgetting grad_accum interaction with pipeline PP micro-batches
incorrect global batch size causing suboptimal LR schedule
gradient norm accumulation bug causing wrong effective LR
acceptance_tests: global batch size matches target token count per step
loss curve matches reference with equivalent global batch

nodes.definition: Enable selective recomputation of activations during backward pass (trading compute for memory) to reduce activation memory from O(seq_len×layers) to O(sqrt(layers)) or per-checkpoint-segment.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Reduces activation memory by 5-10× enabling longer contexts or larger batches
pros.example: seq_len 8192 becomes feasible with full checkpointing on A100 40GB

cons.claim: Full checkpointing adds ~33% compute overhead; selective checkpointing reduces this to 5-10%
cons.example: recomputing attention doubles FLOPs for that layer

failure_modes: applying checkpointing to layers already covered by flash-attn (double overhead)
incorrect checkpoint segment boundaries causing memory spike
checkpointing disabled silently in some framework integrations
acceptance_tests: activation memory reduced by >50% vs no-checkpointing baseline
throughput loss within target budget (<15%)

nodes.definition: Engineer data pipeline to feed GPU with tokenized batches at target throughput: sharded dataset format (WebDataset/MDS), prefetching, worker count tuning, and CPU-GPU transfer overlap.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Data-starved GPU is wasted money; proper pipeline maintains >95% GPU util
pros.example: WebDataset streaming from GCS sustains 800 samples/s on 8×H100

cons.claim: Overprovisioned workers waste CPU/RAM without GPU benefit
cons.example: 256 workers on 8-GPU node adds RAM pressure with no throughput gain

failure_modes: data pipeline bottleneck masking GPU underutilization
tokenization on critical path (should be pre-tokenized)
sharding imbalance causing some workers to stall
acceptance_tests: GPU utilization >90% during data-loading phases
pipeline throughput exceeds GPU consumption rate by 20%
revisit_triggers: dataset size changes order of magnitude

nodes.definition: Schedule concurrent fine-tuning jobs across a shared GPU cluster: time-slicing vs spatial partitioning, priority queuing, GPU-memory-aware placement, and fair-share resource allocation.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Increases cluster utilization from 40% to 80%+ vs serial queuing
pros.example: gang scheduling on Slurm with GPU-aware bin-packing achieves 78% util

cons.claim: Gang scheduling deadlock risk when multiple large jobs compete for partial resources
cons.example: two 8-GPU jobs each waiting for 8 GPUs cause deadlock in 16-GPU cluster

failure_modes: gang deadlock from partial resource allocation
ignoring NVLink locality in placement causing IB bottleneck
preempting long jobs too aggressively causing repeated restarts
acceptance_tests: no deadlock in 24h cluster simulation with mixed job sizes
average cluster utilization >70% under mixed load

nodes.definition: Choose and configure intra-node (NVLink/NVSwitch) and inter-node (InfiniBand 400Gb vs RoCE) networking to match all-reduce and all-gather communication patterns for chosen parallelism strategy.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Correct topology config unlocks 3-8× communication throughput vs misconfigured default
pros.example: NCCL with rail-optimized IB achieves 380 Gb/s vs 120 Gb/s with wrong topology file

cons.claim: Cloud providers abstract topology; actual bandwidth often 60-80% of advertised
cons.example: AWS EFA on p4d achieves 380 Gb/s aggregate but per-flow limited

failure_modes: wrong NCCL topology file causing tree instead of ring all-reduce
PCIe bottleneck for NVLink-capable nodes due to wrong device mapping
ignoring RDMA routing for multi-rail InfiniBand
acceptance_tests: NCCL bandwidth test achieves >80% of theoretical peak
all-reduce time matches predicted communication volume / bandwidth

nodes.definition: Integrate FlashAttention-2/3 to replace standard attention: O(N) memory vs O(N²), higher arithmetic intensity, fused softmax+dropout, and support for variable-length sequences and sliding-window attention.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: 2-4× memory reduction and 2-3× speedup for long sequences; near-mandatory for >4K context
pros.example: FlashAttn-2 reduces A100 memory for 8K context by 8×

cons.claim: Version-specific bugs and limited support for non-standard attention patterns
cons.example: FlashAttn causal mask bug in early v2 releases with GQA

failure_modes: kernel version mismatch with transformer architecture
incorrect causal mask causing non-causal attention
sequence packing length computation error
acceptance_tests: attention output matches standard attention within 1e-3 tolerance
memory use matches FlashAttn theoretical O(N) scaling
revisit_triggers: sequence length increases beyond current kernel support
new attention variant (GQA/MLA) requires kernel update
new GPU generation with different SRAM size

nodes.definition: Apply torch.compile (Dynamo+Inductor) for graph-level fusion, operator reduction, and autotuned triton kernels; manage compile modes (default/reduce-overhead/max-autotune) and dynamic shape handling.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: 10-30% throughput improvement with zero code change for many transformer architectures
pros.example: torch.compile on LLaMA-2 7B achieves 20% tokens/sec improvement

cons.claim: Graph breaks from dynamic control flow silently fall back to eager mode with no speedup
cons.example: data-dependent if-statements cause graph breaks every step

failure_modes: undetected graph breaks eliminating all compile benefit
dynamic shape recompilation on every batch
incompatibility between torch.compile and FSDP in older PyTorch
acceptance_tests: graph break count =0 in compile trace for standard forward pass
throughput improvement >5% vs eager baseline
revisit_triggers: model code changes introducing dynamic control flow

nodes.definition: Apply QLoRA (4-bit NF4 base model + bf16 LoRA adapters) or full QAT to dramatically reduce VRAM for fine-tuning while preserving accuracy via double quantization and paged optimizers.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Enables fine-tuning 70B model on single 80GB GPU; 4× VRAM reduction vs bf16
pros.example: QLoRA 70B on A100 80GB: 48GB VRAM vs 140GB for bf16

cons.claim: Quantization introduces accuracy gap vs bf16 full fine-tune; NF4 gap grows with low rank
cons.example: QLoRA 70B underperforms full SFT by 1-3% on domain tasks

failure_modes: dequantization overhead causing 30% throughput loss vs bf16 LoRA
NF4 calibration mismatch for non-Llama architectures
paged optimizer causing CUDA synchronization stalls
acceptance_tests: QLoRA training loss matches bf16 LoRA within 5% at convergence
peak VRAM within 10% of theoretical NF4 estimate
revisit_triggers: accuracy gap found unacceptable for target task

nodes.definition: Select cloud provider (AWS/GCP/Azure/Lambda/CoreWeave) and region based on GPU availability, egress cost, data residency, spot market depth, and enterprise contract leverage.

included: reserved vs spot vs on-demand mix

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: 2-5× cost difference between providers for same GPU; specialist providers (CoreWeave) often cheapest
pros.example: CoreWeave H100 at $2.50/hr vs AWS p4de at $3.20/hr

cons.claim: Specialist providers lack managed services; egress locks data to provider
cons.example: CoreWeave has no managed Kubernetes; data egress costs offset compute savings

failure_modes: ignoring egress costs when data is stored in different region/provider
picking provider without checking actual GPU availability (waitlists exist)
missing enterprise discount opportunity for committed spend
acceptance_tests: cost estimate validated against actual provider pricing page
GPU availability confirmed before committing data migration

nodes.definition: Engineer fault-tolerant distributed training: health checks, elastic agent restart (torchrun/torchelastic), straggler detection, automatic node replacement, and NCCL watchdog timeout configuration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Node failure without automation causes full job failure and wasted GPU-hours
pros.example: elastic restart recovers 8-node job in 4 min vs 2 hr manual restart

cons.claim: Over-aggressive health checks cause false positives preempting healthy jobs
cons.example: NCCL timeout=30s causes spurious restarts on slow all-reduce

failure_modes: NCCL timeout too short causing spurious restarts
missing health check for GPU memory errors (ECC)
no straggler mitigation causing permanent stragglers to stall job
acceptance_tests: simulated node failure recovers within 10 min
MTTR for single-node failure <15 min in production

nodes.definition: Apply Chinchilla compute-optimal scaling (N_opt ∝ sqrt(C), D_opt ∝ sqrt(C)) to choose model size and token budget given compute budget C; project capability gains and diminishing returns.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Prevents over-parameterizing at fixed compute (pre-Chinchilla error)
pros.example: Chinchilla showed GPT-3 was undertrained by 10×; smaller+more-data model better

cons.claim: Chinchilla laws assume clean data and standard architectures; MoE and instruction-tuned models deviate
cons.example: Mixture-of-Experts scaling exponents differ from dense Chinchilla fit

failure_modes: applying Chinchilla exponents without adjusting for data quality
ignoring inference cost (small model + long context may be costlier to serve)
benchmark-to-loss mapping breaks at task saturation
acceptance_tests: recommended (N,D) within 20% of empirically optimal on pilot compute points
scaling projection matches 3 historical data points
revisit_triggers: new scaling law paper updates exponents
architecture changes (MoE, SSM) invalidate dense exponents

nodes.definition: Monitor training loss curves for divergence, spikes, and plateau; configure loss spike recovery (gradient clipping, LR reduction), NaN/Inf detection, and per-layer gradient norm logging.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: GPU pricing or hardware generation changes materially

pros.claim: Early detection of loss spikes saves GPU-hours; gradient clipping prevents divergence
pros.example: loss spike detected at step 2400; rollback to step 2000 checkpoint saved 12 GPU-hours

cons.claim: Loss monitoring without root-cause tooling leaves engineers blind to cause
cons.example: loss spike seen but unclear if data batch, LR, or numerical issue

failure_modes: gradient clipping too aggressive (clipping every step) masking LR issues
no per-layer norm logging making root cause diagnosis impossible
alert fatigue from too-sensitive thresholds
acceptance_tests: loss spike detected and recovery checkpoint loaded within 30 min
gradient norm alerts correctly identify pathological layers in 3/3 test cases

edges.resolution_rule: prefer spot with elastic restart; on-demand fallback only when preemption rate>30%/hr
use QLoRA only when VRAM is hard constraint; prefer bf16 full fine-tune when VRAM permits
start with ZeRO-3 only; add tensor/pipeline parallelism only if ZeRO-3 throughput <35% MFU
validate torch.compile+FSDP compatibility on target PyTorch version before production
disable manual activation checkpointing for attention layers when using FlashAttn (handles internally)

conflict_axes.name: memory_vs_throughput
conflict_axes.description: Techniques that reduce VRAM (grad checkpointing, ZeRO-3, QLoRA) increase recompute overhead and reduce throughput; throughput-maximizing configs require more VRAM.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use VRAM floor from GPU_SIZING to determine minimum memory target, then optimize throughput within that constraint

conflict_axes.name: cost_vs_reliability
conflict_axes.description: Spot/preemptible instances reduce cost by 60-90% but increase job failure probability; on-demand provides SLA but is expensive.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use spot for >72hr training with checkpoint-on-preemption; switch to on-demand for jobs <4hr or deadline-critical

conflict_axes.name: parallelism_complexity_vs_scale
conflict_axes.description: Higher parallelism degrees (3D parallelism) enable larger models and more GPUs but exponentially increase debugging complexity and communication overhead.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: prefer ZeRO-3 data-parallel until model exceeds 2× GPU VRAM; add tensor parallelism only within node (NVLink); add pipeline parallelism last

conflict_axes.name: quantization_accuracy_vs_vram
conflict_axes.description: Lower bit-width quantization (4-bit NF4 vs bf16) halves VRAM but introduces accuracy gap that grows with reduced LoRA rank.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use QLoRA only when model does not fit in bf16; measure accuracy gap on validation set before committing to quantized training

conflict_axes.name: spot_market_depth_vs_cluster_size
conflict_axes.description: Large multi-node spot jobs require simultaneous availability of many GPUs; spot market depth may not support gang-scheduling requirements.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use spot for single-node or small 2-4 node jobs; use on-demand for jobs requiring >8 nodes to avoid gang-scheduling failures

conflict_axes.name: checkpoint_frequency_vs_storage_cost
conflict_axes.description: More frequent checkpoints reduce recovery loss from preemption but multiply storage cost for large models.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: checkpoint every 500-1000 steps for spot jobs; delete all but last 3 checkpoints; use async save to minimize overhead

conflict_axes.name: scaling_law_vs_inference_cost
conflict_axes.description: Chinchilla-optimal training favors smaller models trained on more data, but inference cost scales with model size; larger undertrained models may serve cheaper.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: compute total cost = training_cost + inference_cost × expected_requests; optimize combined cost not training cost alone

conflict_axes.name: compile_optimization_vs_debugging
conflict_axes.description: torch.compile provides throughput gains but makes training stack traces opaque and graph breaks silent; reduces debuggability.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: enable torch.compile only after loss curve is stable; maintain eager-mode fallback for debugging sessions

conflict_axes.name: cluster_utilization_vs_job_latency
conflict_axes.description: Packing many small jobs increases cluster utilization but increases queue wait times for large priority jobs; priority inversion risk.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: use fair-share priority with reservation windows for large jobs; preempt low-priority jobs only after 2× expected queue time

conflict_axes.name: data_pipeline_cpu_vs_gpu_balance
conflict_axes.description: Under-provisioned data pipeline starves GPU; over-provisioned pipeline wastes CPU/memory with no GPU benefit.
conflict_axes.resolution_heuristic: profile GPU idle time during dataloading phase; scale workers until GPU idle time <5% then stop adding workers

edge_cases.title: VRAM_OOM_at_first_step
edge_cases.description: Training crashes with OOM on step 1 despite VRAM calculation showing fit; cause is activation memory underestimate or optimizer state materialization spike.
edge_cases.trigger: gradient accumulation step 1 peak differs from steady-state estimate
edge_cases.resolution: profile with torch.cuda.memory_summary at step 1; enable gradient checkpointing; reduce micro-batch by 50% as emergency fix

edge_cases.title: NaN_loss_from_fp16_overflow
edge_cases.description: Training loss becomes NaN at step N due to fp16 gradient overflow; undetected without loss monitoring; switch to bf16 or add loss scaling.
edge_cases.trigger: large logit variance in model (e.g. deep networks without pre-norm)
edge_cases.resolution: switch to bf16; if stuck with fp16, enable GradScaler with initial_scale=2^16 and growth_interval=2000

edge_cases.title: silent_throughput_regression_from_graph_break
edge_cases.description: torch.compile graph break causes silent fallback to eager mode; MFU drops 25% with no error message; detected only via MFU monitoring.
edge_cases.trigger: model code changed introducing data-dependent control flow
edge_cases.resolution: run torch._dynamo.explain(model)(batch) to enumerate graph breaks; refactor or use fullgraph=False with break logging

edge_cases.title: checkpoint_corruption_on_preemption
edge_cases.description: Async checkpoint write interrupted mid-write by spot preemption; corrupt checkpoint detected only at next restore attempt.
edge_cases.trigger: preemption signal arrives during async checkpoint save
edge_cases.resolution: use atomic write (write to temp file, rename on complete); validate checksum on save; keep last 2 checkpoints as fallback

edge_cases.title: nccl_hang_from_topology_mismatch
edge_cases.description: NCCL hangs indefinitely on all-reduce due to topology file mismatch; no error message; detected only via NCCL watchdog timeout.
edge_cases.trigger: cluster topology changed but NCCL topo file not updated
edge_cases.resolution: set NCCL_DEBUG=INFO; regenerate topology file; set NCCL_TIMEOUT=300 to get actionable timeout error

edge_cases.title: gang_scheduling_deadlock
edge_cases.description: Two large training jobs each partially allocated GPUs wait for remaining GPUs indefinitely, causing cluster deadlock.
edge_cases.trigger: multi-node jobs submitted simultaneously to under-resourced cluster
edge_cases.resolution: implement all-or-nothing gang scheduling; use backfill scheduling with preemption; set gang reservation timeout

edge_cases.title: data_pipeline_bottleneck_masking_gpu_idle
edge_cases.description: GPU shows 100% utilization in nvidia-smi but MFU is 20%; data loading is serialized between GPU steps causing hidden idle time.
edge_cases.trigger: datasets stored on network storage with high latency; too few dataloader workers
edge_cases.resolution: profile with CUDA events to separate compute from idle; prefetch 2+ batches; cache dataset to local NVMe

edge_cases.title: spot_price_spike_exceeding_on_demand
edge_cases.description: Spot instance price temporarily exceeds on-demand price during peak demand; auto-scaling continues using spot at higher cost than on-demand.
edge_cases.trigger: cloud provider demand surge in target availability zone
edge_cases.resolution: set max spot bid at 90% of on-demand price; implement price monitoring with automatic switch to on-demand fallback

edge_cases.title: qlora_dequantization_throughput_collapse
edge_cases.description: QLoRA training achieves lower tokens/sec than bf16 LoRA despite VRAM savings; 4-bit dequantization kernel is memory-bandwidth bottleneck.
edge_cases.trigger: small batch size causing dequant overhead to dominate; bitsandbytes version without fused kernels
edge_cases.resolution: upgrade to latest bitsandbytes with fused dequant; increase batch size to amortize dequant cost; consider bf16 LoRA if VRAM permits

edge_cases.title: scaling_law_breakdown_on_instruction_tuning
edge_cases.description: Chinchilla compute-optimal model underperforms on instruction-following benchmarks vs smaller model with more RLHF data; scaling law fit on pretraining loss does not transfer.
edge_cases.trigger: evaluating instruction-tuned models on MMLU/MT-Bench vs pretraining loss minimization
edge_cases.resolution: separate pretraining scaling from fine-tuning scaling; measure downstream task performance directly on pilot scale

edge_cases.title: pipeline_parallelism_bubble_exceeding_20pct
edge_cases.description: Pipeline parallel schedule achieves <80% GPU utilization due to pipeline bubble; bubble fraction = (PP-1)/(micro_batches_per_step); too few micro-batches.
edge_cases.trigger: pipeline depth PP=8 with only 4 micro-batches per step gives 46% bubble
edge_cases.resolution: increase micro-batches to >=4×PP; use interleaved 1F1B schedule; reduce PP depth if model fits with ZeRO-3 only

edge_cases.title: fp8_calibration_underflow_on_h100
edge_cases.description: FP8 training via Transformer Engine causes loss spike or NaN at initialization due to incorrect scale calibration; rare but silent.
edge_cases.trigger: initial scale estimate based on few warmup steps; outlier activations outside fp8 range
edge_cases.resolution: use delayed scaling with window=16 steps; monitor amax history; fall back to bf16 for first 100 steps

workflow.name: define_compute_budget_and_model_size
workflow.description: Set total compute budget ($ or GPU-hours), apply Chinchilla to derive compute-optimal (N,D); define model size.
workflow.gate: Chinchilla projection within 20% of pilot measurements

workflow.name: compute_vram_budget_and_select_gpu
workflow.description: Run VRAM math formula for chosen N, seq_len, batch; select GPU type and count; verify cost-per-token.
workflow.gate: VRAM estimate reproduced; cost within budget

workflow.name: select_cloud_provider_and_region
workflow.description: Compare providers on GPU availability, egress cost, spot depth; negotiate enterprise discount; confirm data residency.
workflow.gate: GPU type available in chosen region; cost estimate validated

workflow.name: configure_parallelism_strategy
workflow.description: Choose ZeRO stage or FSDP policy; add tensor/pipeline parallelism only if model exceeds ZeRO-3 VRAM budget; configure network topology.
workflow.gate: NCCL bandwidth test >80% peak; MFU >35% on pilot run

workflow.name: configure_mixed_precision_and_kernels
workflow.description: Set AMP dtype (bf16 preferred); integrate FlashAttention; enable torch.compile; verify no NaN in 100-step pilot.
workflow.gate: Loss matches fp32 baseline within 1%; no NaN in 500 steps

workflow.name: configure_gradient_accumulation_and_checkpointing
workflow.description: Set micro-batch and grad_accum_steps for target global batch; enable activation checkpointing if needed; verify effective batch size.
workflow.gate: Global batch size matches target; VRAM within budget

workflow.name: setup_checkpointing_and_fault_tolerance
workflow.description: Configure checkpoint frequency, async save, restore validation; set up elastic restart and health checks; test preemption recovery.
workflow.gate: Simulated preemption recovers within 10 min; checkpoint restore produces identical loss

workflow.name: setup_data_pipeline
workflow.description: Shard dataset to WebDataset/MDS format; configure prefetch and worker count; benchmark pipeline throughput vs GPU consumption.
workflow.gate: Pipeline throughput exceeds GPU consumption by 20%; GPU idle <5%

workflow.name: configure_monitoring_and_alerting
workflow.description: Set up loss curve monitoring, MFU dashboard, gradient norm logging, NaN detection, and cost burn-rate alerts.
workflow.gate: Loss spike detected in <30 min in test; MFU alert fires on 20% regression

workflow.name: launch_and_validate_training_run
workflow.description: Launch training; monitor first 1000 steps for loss trajectory, MFU, VRAM, cost burn rate; compare against SCALING_LAW projection.
workflow.gate: Loss on track with projection; MFU >35%; cost burn within budget

workflow.name: multi_model_scheduling_setup
workflow.description: Configure cluster scheduler for concurrent fine-tuning jobs with GPU-aware placement, priority queuing, and fair-share allocation.
workflow.gate: Cluster utilization >70%; no deadlock in 24h simulation

workflow.name: cost_effectiveness_review_and_iteration
workflow.description: After run completion or major milestone, re-evaluate cost-per-quality-point; decide whether to scale up, change GPU type, or adjust parallelism.
workflow.gate: Cost-per-quality-point within 25% of projection; decision logged

dominance_rules.name: vram_math_before_gpu_purchase
dominance_rules.rule: Always run VRAM_MATH before GPU_SIZING commitment; never size GPU fleet from parameter count alone.

dominance_rules.name: bf16_over_fp16_for_large_models
dominance_rules.rule: Prefer bf16 over fp16 for models with >7B parameters; fp16 overflow risk outweighs marginal throughput difference.

dominance_rules.name: zero3_before_tensor_parallel
dominance_rules.rule: Exhaust ZeRO-3 (or FSDP FULL_SHARD) options before adding tensor or pipeline parallelism; simpler to debug and nearly equivalent memory savings.
dominance_rules.condition: model fits on single node with ZeRO-3

dominance_rules.name: flash_attn_mandatory_for_long_context
dominance_rules.rule: FlashAttention is non-optional for sequence lengths >2048; standard attention O(N^2) memory makes longer contexts infeasible.

dominance_rules.name: chinchilla_over_intuition_for_compute_allocation
dominance_rules.rule: Use Chinchilla scaling law to set (N,D) for any run >10^21 FLOP; intuition-based sizing is reliably suboptimal.

dominance_rules.name: checkpoint_on_preemption_mandatory_for_spot
dominance_rules.rule: Checkpoint-on-preemption is non-negotiable for spot training jobs; absence makes spot economically worse than on-demand due to full restart loss.

dominance_rules.name: mfu_monitoring_required_before_scaling
dominance_rules.rule: Measure MFU before scaling to more GPUs; low MFU (<30%) indicates config bug that scaling will not fix and will amplify cost.

dominance_rules.name: atomic_checkpoint_writes
dominance_rules.rule: All checkpoint writes must be atomic (write-then-rename); non-atomic writes on spot machines cause silent corruption that manifests only at restore time.

dominance_rules.name: loss_monitor_before_compile
dominance_rules.rule: Establish loss curve baseline in eager mode before enabling torch.compile; compile graph breaks can silently produce incorrect results.

dominance_rules.name: qlora_only_when_vram_constrained
dominance_rules.rule: Use QLoRA only when the full bf16 LoRA model does not fit; prefer bf16 LoRA when VRAM permits to avoid accuracy gap.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_change_parallelism_after_cost_commitment
anti_rework_rules.rule: Finalize parallelism strategy before committing to reserved GPU instances; changing from ZeRO-3 to 3D parallelism requires software re-architecture.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_tune_lr_before_batch_size_fixed
anti_rework_rules.rule: Fix global batch size before tuning LR schedule; LR optimal value scales with sqrt(batch_size) under linear warmup.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_move_data_before_provider_locked
anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm cloud provider and region before migrating training data; cross-provider egress costs can exceed training compute cost.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_upgrade_framework_mid_run
anti_rework_rules.rule: Pin PyTorch and DeepSpeed versions for the duration of a training run; mid-run upgrades cause checkpoint incompatibility.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_change_dtype_mid_training
anti_rework_rules.rule: Mixed precision dtype (bf16/fp16/fp8) must be fixed before training starts; changing dtype mid-run invalidates optimizer state.

anti_rework_rules.name: validate_checkpoint_restore_before_long_run
anti_rework_rules.rule: Always test checkpoint save-restore cycle on a 100-step pilot before launching multi-day training; silent restore bugs waste entire run.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_skip_nccl_bandwidth_test
anti_rework_rules.rule: Run NCCL bandwidth test on actual cluster before multi-node training; topology file misconfiguration causes 3-5x throughput loss that is hard to diagnose later.

anti_rework_rules.name: profile_data_pipeline_before_gpu_scaling
anti_rework_rules.rule: Profile data pipeline throughput vs GPU consumption before scaling GPU count; data-bound jobs do not benefit from more GPUs.

anti_rework_rules.name: do_not_apply_qlora_without_accuracy_validation
anti_rework_rules.rule: Validate QLoRA accuracy on task-specific eval before committing training budget; accuracy gap may require falling back to bf16 full fine-tuning.

iteration_protocol.trigger: MFU falls below 30% on any training run
iteration_protocol.action: profile bottleneck source (compute/memory/communication); fix before scaling GPU count

iteration_protocol.trigger: training loss spike or NaN detected
iteration_protocol.action: rollback to last valid checkpoint; diagnose (gradient norm, batch anomaly, dtype overflow); resume
switch to on-demand or increase checkpoint frequency to every 200 steps
enable gradient checkpointing; reduce micro-batch; verify VRAM math formula
audit MFU, GPU type selection, parallelism overhead; consider switching provider or GPU type

iteration_protocol.trigger: new GPU generation becomes available at lower cost
iteration_protocol.action: re-run VRAM math and cost model for new GPU; compare MFU on pilot run before committing
re-run VRAM math; re-validate FlashAttn compatibility; re-profile MFU
review scheduler config for gang deadlock; audit job queue for priority inversion; tune fair-share weights

iteration_protocol.trigger: Chinchilla scaling projection misses by >30% at intermediate compute point
iteration_protocol.action: run additional pilot points; check data quality and architecture assumptions; consider architecture-specific exponents

iteration_protocol.trigger: torch.compile throughput improvement <5% or causes regression
iteration_protocol.action: enumerate graph breaks; profile eager vs compiled step; disable compile if debugging needed

priority_rationale: VRAM_MATH and GPU_SIZING are gating: wrong sizing causes OOM or budget failure before training starts. COST_MODEL and SCALING_LAW inform all GPU decisions. MIXED_PREC and ZERO_SHARDING are near-universal enablers. FLASH_ATTN is mandatory for long context. CKPT_INFRA is critical for any spot-based run. LOSS_MONITOR prevents GPU-hour waste on diverging runs.
